35/G.goal: Explain the user-centered process of identifying and specifying usability requirements for an interactive system, from lifecycle positioning and requirement classification to contextual inquiry of specified users.
35/G.achieves: Provides the learner with the foundational requirement-gathering skill needed to start the XR case study with user-centered usability requirements that guide later design and implementation.

35/O1.goal: Frame requirement gathering as the user-centered stage of interactive system development where end-user usability requirements are identified.
35/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a user-needs basis for beginning an XR system rather than starting from technical or system capabilities.

35/O2.goal: Distinguish end-user usability requirements from feasibility, interface design, and code design decisions by characterizing them as non-functional interface-quality requirements for interactive systems used by non-experts.
35/O2.achieves: Lets the learner focus requirement work on the usability issues that must be addressed before system design and implementation in the XR case study.

35/O3.goal: Describe how contextual inquiry gathers usability requirements from specified users in a context of use and yields essential features from observed user activities.
35/O3.achieves: Gives the learner a user-centered method for discovering the features and constraints that should drive design refinement in the XR case study.
